# Files that are corrupt on purpose in the pinned upstream archives.
#
# The corpus run treats a `failed` status as an error unless the file name
# matches a pattern below. Every entry names a file that a human has confirmed
# to be broken upstream; a broad pattern would hide real regressions, so the gate
# also warns when an entry stops matching anything.
#
# Nothing else may appear here. A valid file that fails is a bug in Tzim.
#
# Two kinds of entry exist, and they are not the same thing:
#
#   broken  — the bytes violate the format. Tzim refuses the file and says so.
#             libjpeg and Pillow often accept these by concealing the damage
#             (resynchronising at the next marker, guessing the pixel value).
#             Tzim will not: repairing a file is a lossy decision.
#
#   refused — the file is fine but uses a construct the handler declines, such
#             as a progressive scan. These are reported as `skipped`, not
#             `failed`, so they do not need an entry here.
#
# Format: one shell glob matched against the corpus file name (basename).

# --- Pillow 11.3.0, Tests/images -------------------------------------------
# PNG fixtures for Pillow's own error handling.
pillow-broken.png
pillow-broken_data_stream.png
pillow-truncated_end_chunk.png
pillow-truncated_image.png
pillow-apng_syntax_num_frames_zero.png
pillow-unknown_compression_method.png
pillow-tRNS_null_1x1.png

# JPEG fixtures with damage that libjpeg conceals. ImageMagick reports them as
# "Corrupt JPEG data: N extraneous bytes before marker", which is the same
# conclusion this project reaches by a different route.
pillow-truncated_jpeg.jpg
pillow-truncated_app14.jpg
pillow-hopper_bad_exif.jpg
pillow-jpeg_ff00_header.jpg
pillow-junk_jpeg_header.jpg
pillow-photoshop-200dpi-broken.jpg
pillow-ultrahdr.jpg
